messages:
alex g: Heads up — saw a canary spike where ~3% of function/invoke responses are failing output validation and surfacing in the console as 502s. Also being counted towards customer usage. Example below.

sana r: dropping a sample we saw:
```json
{
  "model_response": ["result1", "result2"]
}
```
This should have been `{"result": { ... } }` according to the hook contract.

kevin m: Is this the strict validator rollout (validator v2) that enforces object shapes for action hooks?

jamie: Yes — we toggled strict_mode=true for the canary slice. The model sometimes emits a bare array or a string when it gets confused by the prompt.

kevin m: Two immediate UX/billing issues: (1) console shows a 502 which is confusing for customers, no useful example of the rejected output. (2) tokens still get charged even though we didn't deliver valid structured output.

alex g: I think we should avoid charging customers for validation-only rejects. Proposal: tag those requests as `validation_failure` and retro-zero-out billed tokens in billing pipeline if final consumer did not receive valid output.

sana r: Agreed on billing. Also console UX: instead of a bare 502, show the raw model output and a one-click toggle "show raw" + a short hint about the expected schema. Right now the dashboard only increments a single opaque counter.

jamie: Implementation note — billing currently captures token counts at dispatch time. We can tag the event in telemetry with `reject_reason=shape` and `final_status=rejected` and then the billing backfill job can exclude those at invoice time. That requires a small change to the billing attribution pipeline.

kevin m: Routing policy question: why are these requests not falling back to the permissive variant? Shouldn't we try a permissive parser/model variant before hard failing? That would reduce hard-rejects at cost of slightly lower quality.

alex g: Agreed. Proposed routing order update: exact_variant -> permissive_variant -> degen_fallback -> user_error. We can make that configurable per-route. Tradeoff is additional latency for some calls.

jamie: We can also add a `coerce_on_read` option where the validator will attempt light coercions (wrap bare arrays into `{items: [...]}`, coerce numeric strings) and mark the call as `coerced=true` in telemetry. That keeps customers online while surfacing quality regressions.

sana r: For the console/dashboard we should add: `validation_reject_rate`, `coerced_rate`, `validator_latency_ms`, and `billing_adjustments` panels. Also set an alert: if `validation_reject_rate > 0.5%` in prod for 10m, page the oncall.

kevin m: I'll take a small PR to change the routing order + add the `reject_reason` telemetry tag. Jamie, can you own the console changes to show raw output + hint? Alex, can you own the billing backfill/attribution change and a short playbook entry?

jamie: sgtm. For canary we should enable `coerce_on_read` with sampling=10% in prod routes so we can watch `coerced_rate` and customer impact before wider rollout.

alex g: Sounds good. Ops-bot — can we schedule a controlled rollout window for these config changes?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Rolling rollout scheduled for 2026-03-25 03:00 UTC. Changes: validator v2 -> coerce_on_read=on (canary), routing-fallback=permissive (configurable per-route). Owner: kevin m. Deploy link: https://deploys.internal/6529991234

alex g: Thanks — I'll watch the validator dashboard and post a 24h follow-up with metrics.
